source.title: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text

page_placements.theme: Probe and retrieval information loss is task dependent

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs to form a sparse communication channel and reports its performance, but does not measure or test the SAE reconstruction error properties in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for SAE encode–decode communication, not for the residual reconstruction error itself. It does not measure error predictability, per-token error norms, same-context failure across SAE sizes, comparisons with random errors, or whether adding the error term restores behavior. The paper’s text-round-trip feature survival results concern features replaced when contextual inputs are serialized as concept names, not SAE reconstruction error.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained Llama 3.1 8B SAE as a compression bottleneck for inter-agent communication. It reports only channel fidelity, retrieval and task accuracy. It never measures the SAE error vector: not its linear predictability, its norm scaling across SAE sizes, its loss effect against random errors, or its role in circuit or steering analyses. The comparisons of SAE reconstruction with dense vectors use geometric probe and retrieval measures in a communication setting, not model loss or model behaviour. That is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude the SAE-sparse channel keeps near-perfect probe accuracy at 28x compression. They also conclude that Llama-Mistral representations are Procrustes-alignable, that the text channel matches or beats the latent channels on all tested tasks, and that features lost in text round-trips carry surface form, so latent augmentation adds nothing. They draw no conclusions about SAE reconstruction error.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pretrained SAEs to encode and decode activations as a communication bottleneck, then evaluates channel fidelity and task retrieval. It does not use the error-vector analyses or interventions described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by task subtype and by the number of Procrustes anchors; the study also notes differences between prompt-averaged and single-prompt sender representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing dense layer-23 activations with SAE encode-decode reconstructions barely changes linear-probe concept discrimination: 99.4% vs 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For concept-identity information read by linear probes, discarding the SAE error term costs little (Llama 3.1 8B, layer 23, 131K-latent SAE).

fits_no_version.finding: After Procrustes mapping to Mistral, SAE reconstructions match dense vectors on 112 disambiguation tasks: 67.9% vs 67.0% overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction without the error term preserves the concept signal used in nearest-neighbour cross-model retrieval on these tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: In held-out cross-architecture top-1 retrieval, SAE reconstructions trail dense vectors by about 12 pp: 72.3% vs 84.6% at 100 anchors, 80.0% vs 92.0% at 140.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropping the SAE error term costs a measurable share of cross-model alignable concept signal in fine-grained retrieval, unlike the coarser probe tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Injecting SAE-decoded vectors at layer 23 of a neutral prompt yields the correct concept name in 33/84 cases. No dense-injection comparison is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstructions retain enough causal signal to drive concept-name generation in a minority of cases.

record.problems: The study does not test the reconstruction-error claims or compare SAE error with random errors. Its channel and task results concern concept retrieval and communication, rather than model loss or circuit/steering behavior. The authors state that task types are text-expressible and that the evaluation uses small models and a limited concept dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant SAE reconstruction-error results were reported. Text-round-trip feature-survival results were left out because they concern changes between contextual and bare-name encodings, not SAE reconstruction error.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation; not measured.
Per-token error norms, cross-size predictability, same-context failures and persistence with scale; only one SAE is used.
Downstream loss with SAE reconstructions versus norm-matched random errors; not measured.
Decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and their learnability; not done.
Circuit or steering analyses with and without the error term; the study's reconstruction-versus-dense comparisons are retrieval and probe measures, not model behaviour.
Effect of SAE training choices or architectures on error size; not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE is a measurement and compression tool here. The 'feature survival' results compare contextual and bare-name encodings, not reconstruction error, so they were rightly left out. Rows r5 and r6 are the closest to a reconstruction-error cost: about 12 pp in retrieval. That cost appears only under a communication metric. It cannot be mapped onto V5, which concerns circuits and steering of model behaviour, or onto V3, which concerns loss versus random error.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE reconstruction error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token reconstruction-error norms across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
No comparison of model loss after SAE reconstruction versus random errors of the same size.
No separation of error into linear and nonlinear parts, nor tests of feature learning or dictionary learning on those parts.
The study does not test circuit or steering analyses with and without the SAE error term, or measure the share of model behavior those analyses lose.
No test of whether SAE training choices cause the reconstruction error or whether improved architectures or end-to-end training reduce it.

relation.reason: The connection is methodological and contextual: SAE compression and feature analysis. No dark-matter claim version is tested, assumed, or used as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs as communication bottlenecks and measurement instruments, but neither tests nor uses the SAE dark-matter finding. Using an SAE alone does not satisfy T4.

source_check.notes: Feature loss during text round-trips concerns changes between contextual and bare-name encodings, not the SAE reconstruction-error vector. The listed probe and retrieval results do not establish any claim version.
